source.title: Rapidly Adapting Moment Estimation
source.authors: Guoqiang Zhang; K. Niwa; W. Kleijn

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers and reports training and validation performance on natural-label classification and segmentation tasks, using a different optimizer intervention than the claim versions' original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on natural-label tasks. Its discussion of sharp-curvature learning rates cites prior work and is not a result of this study. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, optimizer comparisons under matched broad tuning, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam and RMSprop with stochastic heavy-ball momentum under limited tuning and reports held-out classification accuracy. These comparator results test V4 independently of the proposed RAME method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present RAME as a simple first-moment adaptive method with promising convergence and validation performance relative to SHB, Adam, and RMSprop. They do not conclude that adaptive optimizers generally generalize worse.
record.recipe_differences: Compares a newly proposed adaptive optimizer, RAME, with SHB, Adam, and RMSprop; uses open-source task implementations and selects the best of five tested initial learning rates by validation performance.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and model architecture; RAME q setting; selected initial learning rate. The paper notes RAME performance changes with q and reports task-dependent optimizer comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: RAME improves or matches competitors across the tested tasks; its VGG16 results improve as q increases from 0.125 to 0.25.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed first-moment adaptive optimizer can achieve competitive optimization and validation performance.

fits_no_version.finding: On COCO people segmentation, RAME beats SHB and Adam on loss and IOU; SHB has higher training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects optimization and held-out performance when fine-tuning a pretrained segmentation network.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Optimizer comparison uses five candidate initial learning rates, selecting the one with best validation performance; the text does not report a broad hyperparameter search or repeated-run uncertainty. Most plotted values are figure-only. The VGG16, ResNet20, and MLP experiments use distinct implementations, and results do not isolate an overall generalization gap because training and held-out errors are not compared as a gap metric.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Several figure-based training-loss outcomes are included although they do not directly measure the V4 held-out-performance claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed to fit the training data.
Controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD. The retained accuracy comparisons do not establish whether adaptive methods have equal or better training performance.
Batch-size comparisons and changes to the training recipe that address large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, measured generalization gaps, and comparisons with alternative generalization measures.

missing.what: The RMSprop-versus-SHB final validation-accuracy comparison for ResNet20 is plotted but has no row. Its ordering cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: Each optimizer's initial learning rate was selected from five candidates using validation performance; other optimizer parameters were fixed. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported. The two challenges are condition-specific exceptions to an 'often' claim, not evidence that its overall frequency claim is false. The supplied text preserves plot axes and legends but not readable curves, so no numerical values or additional comparator orderings are inferred.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels are not tested.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures as an architectural-bias test.

The paper tests RAME against SHB, Adam, and RMSprop on several tasks, but not a broad adaptive-versus-SGD benchmark, language tasks, or the effects of extended tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch penalty test.
